scope.content: Historical names, district attestations, population tables and Sherring citation; contextual, no glossed lexical entries.

Every target lexical pronunciation/grammar example, alternatives, complete verb person paradigm, and source-defined expressions. Preserve separately labelled Standard/Old Kanarese/Bijapur/Telugu comparisons as controls or attributed analysis, not Holiya target rows.

evidence: Current languages.csv explicitly identifies Golari as Holiya alternate name.
Glottolog primary language page identifies Holiya/hoy and alternative Golari-Kannada; cites Grierson1906.
p385 explicitly equates Holiya and Golari of these districts; p394 reinforces same for Bhandara.
identity.historical_classification: Kanarese dialect especially close to Bijapur is preserved as Grierson’s classification, not a reassignment to modern Kannada.
identity.district_policy: General chapter examples receive General unless source explicitly assigns district. Two Bhandara texts share one district variety; text number and caste label remain provenance. No Nagpur tag merely from census or prediction.
identity.coordinates: Source gives districts, not exact elicitation points; leave numeric coordinates blank or explicitly label a sourced district approximation qualityC. Nordic21.32,79.55 is not a surveyed site and must not be copied as exact.

critical_controls: Chanda Golar/Golkars speak Telugu per p385; p577 and594 independently reiterate identity with local Telugu/Komtau. Do not map label Golari blindly across volume.
Standard Kanarese, Old Kanarese, Bijapur and Telugu comparison forms retain source labels; no generic shared-scope rule makes them Holiya attestations.
Census tables, English-only free translation, headings and authority prose remain accounted context.

representation.native: p386 explicitly says only Roman version printed; original submitted Devanagari is unavailable here, so Native stays blank. Do not reconstruct.
representation.profile: Preserve literal source vowels, quantities, aspirates, doubled consonants, nasalization, hyphens and Seoni ṛ. Source warns e/o length supplied from Standard Kanarese may be wrong and other quantities inconsistent; do not harmonize or assert phonemic certainty.
representation.source_analysis: Retain qualified Aryan-influence claims, Telugu attribution of yād batinā/vastā, and tentative hōgdhōdun decomposition as attributed analysis. Do not invent donor identities or graph targets.
